defined-ai.why: Pilot. Third-party provider programme next to own collection; public buyer licence and supplier terms.

aws-data-exchange.why: Pilot. The precedent for sharing files in place from the provider's storage, and a full object model. The one cloud exchange taken deep.

nexdata.why: Large image/video catalogue with per-listing samples, public terms, and a creator-licensed video supply claim to test. Datatang is treated as its alias.

futurebeeai.why: Indian vendor: own crowd capture app, off-the-shelf catalogue, buys third-party datasets, public AI data licence and seller page. The nearest Indian operator analogue.

pixta-ai.why: Stock agency turned dataset marketplace, venue model in public terms, published prices, consent warranties on partners, India sub-brand.

shutterstock.why: The largest stock library licensing content for AI training, with a contributor payment scheme; filings available where its site blocks fetching.

wirestock.why: Creator community sold as datasets plus commissioned creation: catalogue and custom from one contributor base.

troveo.why: The largest dedicated video-licensing broker; royalty paid to owners on every re-licence.

protege.why: Rights-holder aggregation with public provider terms, a field-of-use limit and a likeness ban; absorbed Calliope Networks.

opendatabay.why: Closest structural analogue: a third-party dataset marketplace with its whole legal stack public and dated 2026, including a commission schedule.

poseidon.why: Almost DataMind360's operating model: phone capture, QC, pay per accepted clip, off-the-shelf plus custom, exclusive contributor licence.

kled.why: Phone-app contributors whose uploads are resold to AI buyers under an exclusive licence; fast 2026 growth; aggressive terms worth dissecting.

truelabel.why: Delivers into the buyer's bucket; public collector agreement requiring written consent from people depicted; work-for-hire output resold.

luel.why: Listings flagged 'scoped to order' or 'custom' so a catalogue entry is also a spec for new collection; public terms handle erasure after sale.

laion-5b.why: Pilot failure case: takedown of an image dataset and what past holders were told.

appen.why: Listed vendor with an image/video off-the-shelf category; no public licence.

shaip.why: Image/video catalogue with Indian delivery; licence terms not public; reported acquisition to confirm.

crowdworks-a1-data-marketplace.why: Korean listed crowd-data company with its own dataset marketplace.

datacluster-labs.why: Indian crowd-captured image datasets sold off the shelf.

macgence.why: Indian vendor running a 'Data Marketplace' of its own datasets.

ldc.why: Priced catalogue since 1992: public licence tiers by user type.

elra-elda-catalogue.why: Priced catalogue of third-party resources under standard research and commercial licences.

vaisual.why: Published price grid and use-tiered licence with model releases; possibly dormant.

datarade.why: Lead-generation marketplace model: listings drive quote requests, not checkout.

snowflake-marketplace.why: Second cloud exchange, for comparison of listing, private offer and entitlement mechanics.

hugging-face-hub.why: Gated datasets and dataset cards: the de facto listing format buyers know.

getty-images.why: Stock media licensing to AI developers; litigation over training data.

adobe-stock.why: Pays contributors for content used to train its own models.

bee-maps.why: Crowd dashcam imagery with public per-image and per-clip prices.

dataseeds-ai.why: Photo community sold as catalogue and on-demand collection.

karya.why: Indian crowd-data company that pays workers on resale.

empiric-earth.why: Dashcam driving-event video sold from consumer and fleet footage.

build-ai.why: Egocentric factory video released openly as a funnel to paid data.

aikosh.why: India's government dataset platform: the local public alternative a buyer can reach free.

korea-ai-hub.why: Government-commissioned training datasets distributed free, including image and video.

human-native.why: Licensing broker acquired by Cloudflare in January 2026: the exit of a pure-play broker.

twentybn.why: Failure: crowd-captured video datasets whose licensor changed on acquisition.

ibm-diversity-in-faces.why: Failure: a face dataset withdrawn under biometric-privacy suits.

everalbum.why: Failure: photos used for face models without consent; regulator ordered models deleted.

wejo.why: Failure: a neutral data marketplace that went into administration.
